subject: Science
title: Researching a genetic condition
objective_verbatim: Research a genetic condition online; present.
reading_age_est: rough ARI grade 7.34 on 995 pupil-visible words; heuristic age guide 13.34 years, not a formal reading-age test
pupil_words: I am learning to use a named source to present careful facts about a genetic condition.
success_criteria: I can name the condition and source.
I can explain CFTR inheritance without personal details.
I can tell a sourced fact from a guess.

worked_example.full: The NHS card says cystic fibrosis is inherited. Changed CFTR copies come from both parents. One changed copy usually means a carrier; two usually cause the condition. Name the NHS card with each claim.
worked_example.faded: The NHS card says cystic fibrosis is ___. It involves the ___ gene. One changed copy usually means a ___. Source: ___.
worked_example.removed_step: Link the two changed CFTR copies to inheritance rather than contact; name the NHS source.
worked_example.fade_next: Next lesson hide the “source” sentence and ask pupils to identify the named source independently.

cfu.question: Show me: is the genetic cause of cystic fibrosis inherited or passed by brief contact?
cfu.answer: Inherited. This says nothing about infection precautions a person with CF may need.

hinge.question: A fictional family-source card says altered gene copies passed from parents to their child. Which claim does that evidence support?

options.text: A. The altered copies spread through a shared cough.
options.diagnosis: Confuses an inherited CFTR variant with an infection spread by a cough.

options.text: B. The altered copies arose from the child’s wish.
options.diagnosis: Attributes inherited gene copies to a child’s wish instead of parental transmission.

options.text: C. The altered copies were inherited from the parents.
D. The altered copies travelled through drinking water.
options.diagnosis: Confuses inherited gene copies with an environmental exposure through water.

hinge.decision_rule: About 3 in 4 or more right → move on. Otherwise re-model an anonymous one-copy/two-copy card and the named NHS line, then ask the parallel hinge. No automatic mark or saved response.
hinge.parallel_hinge: Another fictional card says altered gene copies were passed through eggs or sperm. Does this support inheritance or person-to-person infection? Answer: inheritance.

misconceptions.misconception: The genetic cause of cystic fibrosis can spread by contact.
misconceptions.spot: Pupil chooses A, treating the altered copies as contagious.
misconceptions.correction: Use the NHS inheritance line: CFTR changes are inherited. Separately, people with CF may need infection-control advice; do not conflate the genetic condition with infections.

misconceptions.misconception: A carrier with one changed copy must have cystic fibrosis.
misconceptions.spot: Pupil chooses C correctly but says one changed copy always means the condition.
misconceptions.correction: Contrast the carrier and two-copy rows in the NHS source card; use “usually” and no real-person claim.

we_do.support: Point to the card’s condition, inheritance and care lines before speaking.
we_do.stretch: Use the card to reject the claim that every carrier has symptoms.

tiers.F: State the condition and one fact with the NHS source named.
tiers.M: Explain CFTR inheritance and separate it from infection.
tiers.H: Revise an unsupported claim with the NHS card.

stems.F: The card says …; the source is …
stems.M: The CFTR change is inherited because …; infection advice is separate because …
stems.H: The claim is not supported by …; I would revise it to …

tiers.go_deeper: Why does one changed copy in this example not justify saying a carrier has the condition?
tiers.early_finisher: Repair a draft saying a CFTR change spreads by touch and outcomes are fixed; source both repairs.

adaptations.cognition_learning: Keep the NHS source-card model in view; remove one cue for We do, then ask pupils to repeat a fresh example without it.
adaptations.communication_interaction: Offer the key word card and a private partner turn before speaking to the group; accept point, sign or AAC.
adaptations.semh: Check in before the top question and hinge; offer a private first answer, agreed pause and one-step return.
adaptations.sensory_physical: Provide an enlarged high-contrast model and keyboard focus; allow speech-to-text or exact scribing.
adaptations.eal: Pre-teach defined science words with examples; let pupils plan in any language while keeping M/H reasoning open.

prompt_ladder: Wait five seconds while pupil finds a source line.
Point to the three labelled parts of the offline card.

Finish one claim and source together, then pupil tries the next one alone.

F.q: What is the condition named on our card?
Which organisation made the source page?

M.a: Changed CFTR copies are inherited from parents.
One changed CFTR copy, usually without the condition.

H.q: Which claim about the genetic condition is unsupported: inherited or caught by contact?
H.a: Catching the genetic condition is incorrect; infection precautions for people with CF are separate.

H.q: Why cite the source beside a claim?
H.a: So another person can check it and its limits.

diagrams.alt: Two carrier parents each have one usual CFTR copy F and one changed copy f. A drawn Punnett square lists FF, Ff, fF and ff as possible combinations.
diagrams.caption: Simplified inheritance model: each parent carries one changed CFTR copy. The four grid squares are possibilities for each pregnancy, not a prediction for a person.
